item.title: Re: Major conceptual rework
item.content:encoded:
I'll try a rewrite based on that idea, since it does sound cool. Not sure I want to have a wide area-of-effect (since that would be sufficiently obnoxious to contain that the Foundation would have just as likely had one of the radio towers shut down), but there are almost certainly some raccoons still out there that were affected before the Foundation moved in and put a building on top of the anomaly. Perhaps even include a suggestion that the effect includes genetic/epigenetic alterations, so that affected specimens can potentially pass it on to their offspring?

Edit: Rewrite complete! I'm tentative about the second part of the last addendum, since it might venture into "too useful" territory. I may pull it depending on what other people think.

item.title: Major conceptual rework
item.content:encoded:
I had a talk with Erk about this on IRC;

here's the log
bleh

<Voct> Erk - you saw my post on the discussion for that RadioKinetic Anomaly ?
<Erk> the newer one voct?
<Voct> yeah
<Voct> Raccoons.
<Voct> picture it
<Voct> a room full of angry caged raccoons
<Voct> all of them talking
<Voct> saying random stuff that they've pulled out of radio communications
<Erk> hahaha
<Erk> Do they have a speaker-crackle voice, or a strange squeaky racoon voice?
<Erk> Like, do they act like speakers for the signal
<Voct> a combination of (the voice of the person who originally spoke it) and (the raccoon growl)
<Erk> That would certainly give the scp a bit more pizzazz
<Voct> oh, and because it affects all raccoons *in the vicinity*
<Voct> once you capture all the raccoons in a given area
<Voct> more will move in
<Voct> so the Foundation has to send people out every night
<Voct> to hunt down all the raccoons in the area
<Erk> Hahaha
<Voct> and check
<Voct> to see if they speak English.
<Erk> Do they remain affected if they leave?
<Erk> I think raccoons that get affected should remain radio receivers
<Erk> maybe less powerful, but they'll still wander around quoting cell phone communications and things
<Erk> At the epicenter they're far more potent though.
<Aelanna> … radio racoons?
<Voct> yeah
<Voct> yeah
<Erk> aelanna, we're figuring how to make !scp-724 actually interesting
<Voct> raccoons that leave the radius of effect will only quote cellphone stuff if they're way close to a transmitter or something?
<Aelanna> I saw that last night
<Voct> hm
<Aelanna> Lei is the original author?
<Voct> Yeah
<Voct> hm
<Voct> maybe they remain receivers, but not speakers?
<Erk> how do you mean? If they don't speak anymore it wouldn't be clear they were receiving would it?
<Voct> Erk - they get all upset if you broadcast static
<cbc> well hey maybe they'll respond and let me do this tongiht?
<Voct> dunno
<Erk> Personally I think it'd be more fun if they just randomly started speaking on occasion.
<Erk> Much more rarely though
<Voct> Erk - it's just stuff they intercept from the radio communication
<Erk> but you're walking outside, taking out the garbage, when suddenly you catch sight of a raccoon in a nearby tree. You make eye contact, and the raccoon stares back. Then it says "Fourteen soldiers were injured today in a suicide bombing."
<Voct> Erk - that's a wonderful image.
<Voct> Erk - I'm thinking of it being called "Radio Receiver Raccoons" ?
<Erk> Voct, I'd say either Radio Raccoons or Receiver Raccoons would be punchier…
<Voct> okay
<Hungry_Man> Radio Raccoons, definitely.
<Erk> The raccoon crews could disguise themselves as homeless people
<Erk> or total rednecks depending on the environment
<Voct> neither homeless nor rednecks would have tranq darts
<Erk> I do wonder if they'd be tranquing the raccoons at this stage… wouldn't they have enough?
<Erk> Oooh
<Erk> unless each raccoon was 'tuned' to a certain frequency when it was exposed to the SCP
<Doc_Kens> Why does this remind me of a Studio Ghibli film?
<Voct> Erk - we don't know. So we keep them.
<Voct> Just in case.
<Erk> so the storage facility consists of rows upon rows of cages labelled with frequencies, each cage containing a raccoon
Voct> a VERY ANGRY raccoon
<Erk> quoting someone's cell conversation
<Voct> don't you love it?
<Erk> "Snarl, hiss. Never call me anymore, why is that. Grrrr. Did the shopping for you yesterday. SPit spit"
<Erk> Or, rather than frequency
<Voct> and then just as the raccoon starts to say something interesting and useful…
<Voct> it stops talking and starts eating.
<Erk> Each raccoon locks onto a specific signal, changing even when that signal is modulated
<Erk> so, like, if it starts picking up the radio transmissions of an al qaeda cell in afghanistan, it will always pick up that cell's transmissions even if they change walkie talkies
<Voct> which is useless unless you have someone who recognizes Pashto
<Voct> and it's all linked back to the nearby confluence of towers
<Erk> Yep. And even then he translates it as "Growl growl, Ahid went to the village and brought back some bread. Snarl. Yeah, I love that bakery too." and then the coon takes a drink.
<Erk> Leading to a massive issue with data sifting
<Voct> Erk - the worst part would be when two raccoons are spouting different sides of the same conversation
<Erk> hah they probably have a few where they've realised they're tuned to people who often talk to each other.
<Erk> so they keep the cages side-by-side
<Voct> and then the raccoons start trying to attack each other through their cages
<Voct> all the while talking romantically to each other
<Erk> I can see the guards now. "Hey, Jim, 0449 and 0450 are fighting again. Want to take bets?" "Oh, sorry Sam, I heard them earlier today. 0449 forgot to pick the kids up from school."
<Erk> "Hey sweety, how was SNARL SNARL GROWL BITE CAGE", "Oh, it was great, I got a RATTLE GROWL SPIT"
<Voct> "Note: yes, the conversations between SCP-724-056 and SCP-724-058 are adorable. But 056 and 058 hate each other and have injured themselves trying to claw their way through the cages."
<Erk> For the sake of humour, SCP infection should make the raccoons more ornery
<Voct> well
<Voct> we're not sure if it's because of the infection
<Voct> or because, y'know
<Voct> they've been captured and are being kept in small cages
<Voct> not *too* small
<Voct> we don't want to risk damaging their health
<Erk> Actually to be a little more scp'ish, maybe receiving radio transmissions is uncomfortable to them as well
<Erk> mildly activating pain centers in the brain consistent with a constant itching sensation
<Voct> Erk - then raccoons wouldn't be constantly entering the territory
<Erk> they wouldn't feel the itch until they'd been infected, though
<Voct> I still don't like it
<Erk> Fair enough.
<Erk> It's also possible that they are constantly itchy, but emitting the radio signals reduces the feeling
<Voct> hmm
<Erk> so infected raccoons tend to return to the area if they are clever enough to make the connection, because it's easier to broadcast there
<Erk> I gotta go though, battery is dead and no plugin
<Erk> ttyl
<Erk> good luck with the crazy coons
<Erk> [having a reason for them to return to the area might be a good plan, because otherwise it's hard to imagine the Foundation being able to keep this one secret]
<Voct> crazy white-trash rednecks babbling about talking raccoons?
<Voct> I think it should just be a reasonably good territory for raccoons to live in
<Voct> no itch, no pain
<Voct> just yummy garbage, safe attics, and the goddamn Foundation shooting them with tranq darts and sticking them in cages.

item.title: Re: Hm
item.content:encoded:
Actually, that's an idea: it manifests via the local raccoons. So the Foundation has to house and contain a raccoon colony.

And the raccoons speak. Instead of the radio signals manifesting in the air, they manifest in the larynges of the raccoons. So if you want to use this for surveillance, you have to go in there and sit among the raccoons with a microphone.

And it keeps affecting new raccoons as they move into the territory.

item.title: Re: Hm
item.content:encoded: Some sort of life-form (sapient or otherwise)? Or maybe the radio anomaly manifests via local fauna?

item.title: Re: Hm
item.content:encoded: Any ideas for ramping up the weird? I'm not particularly attached to the current effect - the cause (seemingly mundane radio signals producing an anomaly) is the part I care about. I just picked the audio effect because it was the least-cliche idea I had.

item.title: Re: Hm
item.content:encoded: That's how I feel as well. I don't have any strong opinions one way or another, this sounds more like a plausible "unexplained mysteries"-style real-world radio anomaly than something that belongs in the SCP database.

item.title: Hm
item.content:encoded: Not weird enough. I'm not downvoting yet, because there's potential for something with the anomaly, but you need to amp the weirdness.
